参加費[さんかひ]：無料[むりょう]（飲[の]み物[もの]は自分[じぶん]で持[も]ってきてください）

translationEn: Would you like to enjoy speaking Japanese with local volunteers? You can practice Japanese useful for daily life, such as everyday shopping and hospital conversations.

Location: International Exchange Center, 2nd Floor, Meeting Room B

items.titleJp: 忘れ物[わすれもの]のお知らせ[しらせ]
items.contextEn: Email from a hotel reception desk to a guest who checked out earlier that morning.
paragraphs: 本日[ほんじつ]は「みなとホテル」にご宿泊[しゅくはく]いただき、誠[まこと]にありがとうございました。お帰[かえ]りのあと、お部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]していたスタッフから、机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に黒[くろ]い充電器[じゅうでんき]が残[のこ]っていたと連絡[れんらく]がありました。

questions.explanationEn: The email clearly states "送料はお客様のご負担となります" (shipping charges are borne by the guest).

items.titleJp: 夜[よる]のジョギングを続[つづ]けるコツ
items.titleEn: My Trick for Sticking With Evening Jogging
items.contextEn: Personal column written by an office worker about building an exercise habit.
paragraphs: 去年[きょねん]まで、私[わたし]は運動[うんどう]を始[はじ]めても、いつも三日[みっか]ぐらいでやめてしまっていました。最初[さいしょ]から「毎日[まいにち]一時間[いちじかん]走[はし]る」という高[たか]すぎる目標[もくひょう]を決[き]めていたからです。

translationEn: Until last year, even when I started exercising, I always quit after about three days. That was because from the very beginning I set an overly high goal of running one hour every day.

So this year I changed my approach. I made a rule: 'Once I get home from work, just put on my running shoes and go outside for only ten minutes.' Thinking it is just a short time puts my mind at ease, and once I start running, more days end up with me running around twenty minutes anyway. Thanks to this, I have kept it up for half a year already.

questions.explanationEn: The writer explicitly blames setting too high a goal from the start (毎日一時間走るという高すぎる目標).

items.titleJp: 日本[にほん]の自動[じどう]販売機[はんばいき]の工夫[くふう]
items.titleEn: Clever Features of Japanese Vending Machines
items.contextEn: Short cultural essay introducing modern features of vending machines in Japan.
paragraphs: 日本[にほん]の町[まち]を歩[ある]くと、駅のホームや道[みち]の角[かど]など、あちこちで自動[じどう]販売機[はんばいき]を見[み]かけます。冷[つめ]たい飲[の]み物[もの]だけでなく、冬[ふゆ]になると温[あたた]かいお茶[ちゃ]やコーンスープも買[か]えてとても便利[べんり]です。

translationEn: When walking through towns in Japan, you spot vending machines everywhere, such as on station platforms and street corners. It is very convenient that you can buy not only cold drinks, but also hot tea and corn soup when winter comes.

Recently, vending machines that help during disasters like earthquakes have also been increasing. Even if the power goes out, people can take out water and tea inside for free, or shelter guidance appears on the screen. Rather than merely selling drinks, they also support community safety.

items.titleJp: 初めて[はじめて]のホームステイで学[まな]んだこと
items.titleEn: What I Learned During My First Homestay
items.contextEn: Reflection written by an exchange student after staying with a Japanese host family.
paragraphs: 先月[せんげつ]、京都[きょうと]のホストファミリーの家[いえ]に二週間[にしゅうかん]泊[と]まりました。最初[さいしょ]は自分[じぶん]の日本語[にほんご]が間違[まちが]っていたら恥[は]ずかしいと思[おも]って、あまり自分[じぶん]から話[はな]しかけられませんでした。

However, one evening my host mother smiled and told me, 'Your Japanese doesn't have to be perfect, so ask as many times as you need when you don't understand.' After that I gradually gathered courage and began talking at the dinner table about my country's food and school. I truly felt that speaking without fearing mistakes is the best way to study.
